[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (3) Subject to paragraphs (7) and (8), where paragraph (1)(a) applies, the court must, unless it considers it unjust to do so, order that the defendant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (a) costs (including any recoverable pre-action costs) from the date on which the relevant period expired; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (b) interest on those costs. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (4) Subject to paragraph (7), where paragraph (1)(b) applies, the court must, unless it considers it unjust to do so, order that the claimant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (a) interest on the whole or part of any sum of money (excluding interest) awarded, at a rate not exceeding 10% above base rate for some or all of the period starting with the date on which the relevant period expired;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (b) costs (including any recoverable pre-action costs) on the indemnity basis from the date on which the relevant period expired;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (c) interest on those costs at a rate not exceeding 10% above base rate; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (d) provided that the case has been decided and there has not been a previous order under this sub-paragraph, an additional amount, which shall not exceed £75,000, calculated by applying the prescribed percentage set out below to an amount which is—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (i) the sum awarded to the claimant by the court; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (ii) where there is no monetary award, the sum awarded to the claimant by the court in respect of costs—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] Amount awarded by the court | Prescribed percentage

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] Up to £500,000 | 10% of the amount awarded

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] Above £500,000 | 10% of the first £500,000 and (subject to the limit of £75,000) 5% of any amount above that figure. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (5) In considering whether it would be unjust to make the orders referred to in paragraphs (3) and (4), the court must take into account all the circumstances of the case including—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (a) the terms of any Part 36 offer;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (b) the stage in the proceedings when any Part 36 offer was made, including in particular how long before the trial started the offer was made;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (c) the information available to the parties at the time when the Part 36 offer was made;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (d) the conduct of the parties with regard to the giving of or refusal to give information for the purposes of enabling the offer to be made or evaluated; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (e) whether the offer was a genuine attempt to settle the proceedings. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (6) Where the court awards interest under this rule and also awards interest on the same sum and for the same period under any other power, the total rate of interest must not exceed 10% above base rate. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (7) Paragraphs (3) and (4) do not apply to a Part 36 offer—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (a) which has been withdrawn;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (b) which has been changed so that its terms are less advantageous to the offeree where the offeree has beaten the less advantageous offer;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (c) made less than 21 days before trial, unless the court has abridged the relevant period. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (8) Paragraph (3) does not apply to a soft tissue injury claim to which rule 36.21 applies. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (Rule 44.2 requires the court to consider an offer to settle that does not have the costs consequences set out in this Section in deciding what order to make about costs.)

## Personal injury claims

## Personal injury claims for future pecuniary loss

## 36.18

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (1) This rule applies to a claim for damages for personal injury which is or includes a claim for future pecuniary loss. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (2) An offer to settle such a claim will not have the consequences set out in this Section unless it is made by way of a Part 36 offer under this rule. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (3) A Part 36 offer to which this rule applies may contain an offer to pay, or an offer to accept—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (a) the whole or part of the damages for future pecuniary loss in the form of—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (i) a lump sum;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (ii) periodical payments; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (iii) both a lump sum and periodical payments;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (b) the whole or part of any other damages in the form of a lump sum. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (4) A Part 36 offer to which this rule applies—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (a) must state the amount of any offer to pay or to accept the whole or part of any damages in the form of a lump sum;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (b) may state—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (i) what part of the lump sum, if any, relates to damages for future pecuniary loss; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (ii) what part relates to other damages to be paid or accepted in the form of a lump sum;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (c) must state what part of the offer relates to damages for future pecuniary loss to be paid or accepted in the form of periodical payments and must specify—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (i) the amount and duration of the periodical payments;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (ii) the amount of any payments for substantial capital purchases and when they are to be made; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (iii) that each amount is to vary by reference to the retail prices index (or to some other named index, or that it is not to vary by reference to any index); and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (d) must state either that any damages which take the form of periodical payments will be funded in a way which ensures that the continuity of payments is reasonably secure in accordance with section 2(4) of the Damages Act 1996 4 or how such damages are to be paid and how the continuity of their payment is to be secured. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (5) Rule 36.6 applies to the extent that a Part 36 offer by a defendant under this rule includes an offer to pay all or part of any damages in the form of a lump sum. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (6) Where the offeror makes a Part 36 offer to which this rule applies and which offers to pay or to accept damages in the form of both a lump sum and periodical payments, the offeree may only give notice of acceptance of the offer as a whole. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (7) If the offeree accepts a Part 36 offer which includes payment of any part of the damages in the form of periodical payments, the claimant must, within 7 days of the date of acceptance, apply to the court for an order for an award of damages in the form of periodical payments under rule 41.8. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.18] (Practice Direction 41B contains information about periodical payments under the Damages Act 1996.)

## Offer to settle a claim for provisional damages

## 36.19

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (1) An offeror may make a Part 36 offer in respect of a claim which includes a claim for provisional damages. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (2) Where the offeror does so, the Part 36 offer must specify whether or not the offeror is proposing that the settlement shall include an award of provisional damages. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (3) Where the offeror is offering to agree to the making of an award of provisional damages, the Part 36 offer must also state—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (a) that the sum offered is in satisfaction of the claim for damages on the assumption that the injured person will not develop the disease or suffer the type of deterioration specified in the offer;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (b) that the offer is subject to the condition that the claimant must make any claim for further damages within a limited period; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (c) what that period is. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (4) Rule 36.6 applies to the extent that a Part 36 offer by a defendant includes an offer to agree to the making of an award of provisional damages. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.19] (5) If the offeree accepts the Part 36 offer, the claimant must, within 7 days of the date of acceptance, apply to the court for an award of provisional damages under rule 41.2. ## Deduction of benefits and lump sum payments

## 36.20

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (1) In this rule and rule 36.11—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (a) “the 1997 Act” means the Social Security (Recovery of Benefits) Act 1997 5 ;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (b) “the 2008 Regulations” means the Social Security (Recovery of Benefits)(Lump Sum Payments) Regulations 2008 6 ;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (c) “recoverable amount” means—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (i) “recoverable benefits” as defined in section 1(4)(c) of the 1997 Act; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (ii) “recoverable lump sum payments” as defined in regulation 1 of the 2008 Regulations;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (d) “deductible amount” means—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (i) any benefits by the amount of which damages are to be reduced in accordance with section 8 of, and Schedule 2 to the 1997 Act 7 (“deductible benefits”); and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (ii) any lump sum payment by the amount of which damages are to be reduced in accordance with regulation 12 of the 2008 Regulations (“deductible lump sum payments”); and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (e) “certificate”—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (i) in relation to recoverable benefits, is construed in accordance with the provisions of the 1997 Act; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (ii) in relation to recoverable lump sum payments, has the meaning given in section 29 of the 1997 Act, as applied by regulation 2 of, and modified by Schedule 1 to, the 2008 Regulations. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (2) This rule applies where a payment to a claimant following acceptance of a Part 36 offer would be a compensation payment as defined in section 1(4)(b) or 1A(5)(b) 8 of the 1997 Act. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (3) A defendant who makes a Part 36 offer must, where relevant, state either—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (a) that the offer is made without regard to any liability for recoverable amounts; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (b) that it is intended to include any deductible amounts. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (4) Where paragraph (3)(b) applies, paragraphs (5) to (9) will apply to the Part 36 offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (5) Before making the Part 36 offer, the offeror must apply for a certificate. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (6) Subject to paragraph (7), the Part 36 offer must state—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (a) the gross amount of compensation;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (b) the name and amount of any deductible amounts by which the gross amount is reduced; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (c) the net amount of compensation. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (7) If at the time the offeror makes the Part 36 offer, the offeror has applied for, but has not received, a certificate, the offeror must clarify the offer by stating the matters referred to in paragraph (6)(b) and (c) not more than 7 days after receipt of the certificate. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (8) For the purposes of rule 36.17(1)(a), a claimant fails to recover more than any sum offered (including a lump sum offered under rule 36.6) if the claimant fails upon judgment being entered to recover a sum, once deductible amounts identified in the judgment have been deducted, greater than the net amount stated under paragraph (6)(c). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (Section 15(2) of the 1997 Act provides that the court must specify the compensation payment attributable to each head of damage. Schedule 1 to the 2008 Regulations modifies section 15 of the 1997 Act in relation to lump sum payments and provides that the court must specify the compensation payment attributable to each or any dependant who has received a lump sum payment.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (9) Where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (a) further deductible amounts have accrued since the Part 36 offer was made; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (b) the court gives permission to accept the Part 36 offer,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] the court may direct that the amount of the offer payable to the offeree shall be reduced by a sum equivalent to the deductible amounts paid to the claimant since the date of the offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.20] (Rule 36.11(3)(b) states that permission is required to accept an offer where the relevant period has expired and further deductible amounts have been paid to the claimant.)

## Miscellaneous

## Cases in which the offeror’s costs have been limited to court fees

## 36.21

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.21] (1) This rule applies in any case where the offeror is treated as having filed a costs budget limited to applicable court fees, or is otherwise limited in their recovery of costs to such fees. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.21] (Rule 3.14 provides that a litigant may be treated as having filed a budget limited to court fees for failure to file a budget.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.21] (2) “Costs” in rules 36.13(5)(b), 36.17(3)(a) and 36.17(4)(b) shall mean—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.21] (a) in respect of those costs subject to any such limitation, 50% of the costs assessed without reference to the limitation; together with

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.21] (b) any other recoverable costs. ## SECTION II Claims to Which Sections VI, VII, or VIII of Part 45 Apply

## Scope of this Section and definitions

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] 36.22. —(1) This Section applies where a claim is one to which Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII of Part 45 applies. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (2) In this Section—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (a)“fixed cost medical report” and “soft tissue injury claim” have the meaning ascribed by paragraph 1.1(10A) and (16A) respectively of the RTA Protocol;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (b)for the purposes of rules 36.23 and 36.24, a defendant’s Protocol offer is either—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (i)defined in accordance with rules 36.26 and 36.27; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (ii)if the claim leaves the Protocol before the Court Proceedings Pack Form is sent to the defendant—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (aa)the last offer made by the defendant before the claim leaves the Protocol; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (bb)deemed to be made on the first business day after the claim leaves the Protocol; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (c)reference to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (i)the “Court Proceedings Pack Form” is a reference to the form used in the Protocol; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Scope of this Section and definitions] (ii)“business day” is a reference to a business day as defined in rule 6.2. ## Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] 36.23 .—(1) Where a Part 36 offer is accepted within the relevant period, the claimant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (a)the fixed costs in Table 12, Table 14 or Table 15 in Practice Direction 45 for the stage applicable at the date on which notice of acceptance was served on the offeror; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (b)any applicable additional fixed costs allowed under Section I, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII of Part 45 incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (2) Where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (a)a defendant’s Part 36 offer relates to part only of the claim; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (b)at the time of serving notice of acceptance within the relevant period the claimant abandons the balance of the claim,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] the claimant is entitled to the fixed costs in paragraph (1). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (3) Subject to paragraphs (4) and (5), where a defendant’s Part 36 offer is accepted after the relevant period—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (a)the claimant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (i)the fixed costs in Table 12, Table 14 or Table 15 in Practice Direction 45 for the stage applicable at the date on which the relevant period expired; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (ii)any applicable additional fixed costs allowed under Section I, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (b)the claimant is liable for the defendant’s costs in accordance with paragraph (8). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (4) Where a claim no longer continues under the RTA or EL/PL Protocol, then, subject to paragraph (5), where the claimant accepts the defendant’s Protocol offer after the date on which the claim leaves the Protocol—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (a)the claimant is entitled to the applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 or Table 11 in Practice Direction 45; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (b)the claimant is liable for the defendant’s costs in accordance with paragraph (8). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (5) In a soft tissue injury claim, if the defendant makes a Part 36 offer before the defendant receives a fixed cost medical report, paragraphs (3) and (4) shall only have effect if the claimant accepts the offer more than 21 days after the defendant received the report. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (6) Fixed costs shall be calculated by reference to the amount of the offer which is accepted. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (7) Where the parties do not agree the liability for costs, the court must make an order as to costs. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (8) Subject to paragraph (9) where the court makes an order for costs in favour of the defendant, the defendant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (a)the fixed costs in Table 12, Table 14 or Table 15 in Practice Direction 45 for the stage applicable at the date of acceptance; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (b)any applicable additional fixed costs allowed under Section I, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] less the fixed costs to which the claimant is entitled under paragraph (3)(a)(i) or (4). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (9) Where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (a)an order for costs is made pursuant to paragraph (3); and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (b)the stage applicable at the date on which the relevant period expires and the stage applicable at the date of acceptance are the same,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] the defendant is entitled to the fixed costs applicable to that stage. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer] (10) The parties are entitled to disbursements allowed in accordance with Section IX of Part 45 incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them. ## Costs consequences following judgment

## 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (2) Subject to paragraphs (3), (4) and (5), where an order for costs is made pursuant to rule 36.17(3)—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (a)the claimant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (i)the fixed costs in Table 12, Table 14 or Table 15 in Practice Direction 45 for the stage applicable at the date on which the relevant period expired; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (ii)any applicable additional fixed costs allowed under Section I, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (b)the claimant is liable for the defendant’s costs in accordance with paragraph (9). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (3) Where rule 36.17(1)(b) applies, the claimant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (a)the fixed costs in Table 12, Table 14 or Table 15 in Practice Direction 45 for the stage applicable at the date of judgment; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (b)any applicable additional fixed costs allowed under Section I, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (4) Where the court makes an order pursuant to rule 36.17(4), instead of costs awarded on the indemnity basis under rule 36.17(4)(b), the claimant is entitled to additional costs in accordance with paragraph (5). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (5) The additional costs are an amount equivalent to 35% of the difference between the fixed costs for—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (a)the stage applicable when the relevant period expires; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (b)the stage applicable at the date of judgment,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] to which the claimant is entitled under paragraph (3)(a) and (b). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (6) Where a claim no longer continues under the RTA or EL/PL Protocol, then, subject to paragraph (7), where the claimant fails to obtain a judgment more advantageous than the defendant’s Protocol offer—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (a)the claimant is entitled to the applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 or Table 11 in Practice Direction 45; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (b)the claimant is liable for the defendant’s costs in accordance with paragraph (9); and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (c)in this rule, the amount of the judgment is less than the Protocol offer where the judgment is less than the offer once deductible amounts identified in the judgment are deducted. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (“Deductible amount” is defined in rule 36.20(1)(d).)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (7) In a soft tissue injury claim, if the defendant makes a Part 36 offer or Protocol offer before the defendant receives a fixed cost medical report, paragraphs (2) and (6) shall only have effect in respect of costs incurred by either party more than 21 days after the defendant received the report. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (8) Fixed costs must be calculated by reference to the amount which is awarded. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (9) Where the court makes an order for costs in favour of the defendant, the defendant is entitled to—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (a)the fixed costs in Table 12, Table 14 or Table 15 in Practice Direction 45 applicable at the date of judgment; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (b)any applicable additional fixed costs allowed under Section I, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] less the fixed costs to which the claimant is entitled under paragraph (2)(a) or (6). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.24. —(1) Rule 36.17 applies with the following modifications.] (10) The parties are entitled to disbursements allowed in accordance with Section IX of Part 45 incurred in any period for which costs are payable to them. ## III RTA PROTOCOL AND EL/PL OFFERS TO SETTLE

## Scope of this Section

## 36.25

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.25] (1) Where this Section applies, Section I and Section II do not apply. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.25] (2) This Section applies to an offer to settle where the parties have followed the RTA Protocol or the EL/PL Protocol and started proceedings under Part 8 in accordance with Practice Direction 49F (“the Stage 3 Procedure”). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.25] (3) A reference to the Court Proceedings Pack Form is a reference to the form used in the relevant Protocol. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.25] (4) Nothing in this Section prevents a party making an offer to settle in whatever way that party chooses, but if the offer is not made in accordance with this Section, it will not have any costs consequences. ## Form and content of a Protocol offer

## 36.26

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.26] (1) An offer to settle which is made in accordance with this rule is called a Protocol offer.
